identity.title: Direct-Vulkan native shell: window, surface, input, IME and accessibility bridge

context_capsule.purpose_for_a_reader_without_history: Small Handshake-owned crates give the kernel-owned native shell its window, Vulkan surface, input, IME and accessibility bridge with no egui, eframe or wgpu, so a zero-egui shell binary can be built beside the current application.

specification_anchor_refs.verbatim: The genuine native Handshake GUI MUST render through a Vulkan-backed path. A DirectX or OpenGL fallback MUST NOT be renamed or accepted as Vulkan.

Renderer adoption MUST consume the centralized GPU ownership and memory contracts in section 15.5. Native window or module clients MUST NOT bypass them through independently owned devices, pools or budgets.
Window creation, resize/recreation and multiwindow use MUST share the authoritative resource/budget/lifecycle contract without treating each window as an independent authority.
The trusted local kernel MAY initialize and render the Vulkan login screen and application shell before account activation only under the exact registered full capability device.gpu.shell.

closure_unit.outcome: Small Handshake-owned crates give the kernel-owned native shell its window, Vulkan surface, input, IME and accessibility bridge with no egui, eframe or wgpu, so a zero-egui shell binary can be built beside the current application.

materialized_acceptance.text: Closure and contracts: each crate builds alone; none of egui, eframe, egui-winit, egui-wgpu, egui_tiles, epaint, ecolor, emath, egui_kittest, kumihimo-egui, cabinet-egui, cabinet-peak-egui, handshake_context_menu_egui, wgpu, wgpu-core, wgpu-hal, glow is in any closure; no winit, ash, accesskit-platform or toolkit type appears in a public signature except the AccessKit core node types in the accessibility crate.

Window: create, show without activation, resize, minimize, restore, move across monitors, per-monitor DPI change, cursor shape, clipboard, OS file drop and close are typed events and commands; a quiet window never takes foreground, focus or a Z-order place above the Operator's window.

Surface: VkSurface and swapchain live on the MT-203 device through an admitted claim; resize, minimize and restore recreate it; an old swapchain and its images are released once, after the owner reports settlement; no vkDeviceWaitIdle on the frame path.
Frames are damage-driven: no redraw without damage, an armed timer or an input; idle submits no GPU work; present mode and frame pacing are reported values, not assumptions.

Input: pointer, wheel, precision touchpad, keyboard (physical and logical key, repeat, dead keys), text and modifiers arrive as typed events tagged with origin (Operator device or model action) and a timestamp; no API injects OS input.

IME: OS composition becomes one typed event stream per focused text target (enabled, preedit with cursor range, commit, cancel, disabled) and the candidate rectangle follows the caret on scroll and DPI change; focus loss sends one cancel or commit, never both. The composition state itself is Kumihimo's (KG-03); this crate holds none.

Accessibility: the host semantic tree reaches UIA with stable node ids across frames, roles, names, values, bounds, text runs, focus and actions; actions come back as typed requests; reading the tree never activates the window; every window has its own tree.
Multiwindow: root, detached panes and detached Settings share one device and one owner ledger; closing one window keeps other windows and in-flight work valid.

Loss and unavailability: device loss rebinds through MT-203 and redraws; a missing or rejected device shows a typed, readable unavailable state and exits with a typed code; no D3D, OpenGL or software fallback exists in the code.

Pre-account startup: the product binary opens the device only under device.gpu.shell and the kernel issuer (NATIVE-RENDER-BOOT-001..008); without both it refuses with a typed outcome. Test binaries say so in their receipts.
Shutdown: explicit close drains, settles claims, acknowledges Palmistry and exits; a crash leaves the OS exception handler and panic hook behaviour unchanged.
Size: five crates (window, surface, input, accessibility, shell); shell is composition only and holds no widget, pane or domain logic; line counts per crate are reported each slice.

implementation_steps.step: S1 (first coding slice): window crate only. Define the typed window event and command enums (no winit type public), quiet create flags, DPI scale events, minimize/restore, multiple windows; implement over winit 0.30.13 kept private; unit tests for event mapping and a focus-ban source scan of this crate. Record in the crate README why raw Win32 was or was not needed.
S2: surface crate: surface and swapchain on the MT-203 lease, acquire, present, resize recreate, occlusion, frame-pacing report; unit tests over a fake owner for settlement ordering.

S3: input crate: pointer, wheel, keyboard, text, modifiers and translation of OS IME events to the typed stream; origin tag; property tests over recorded event sequences (no composition state kept here).

S4: accessibility crate: semantic tree to AccessKit update, action requests back, stable node ids, per-window adapters; decide and record whether the quiet accesskit_windows patch is still required and where it lives.
S5: shell binary: opens under device.gpu.shell, shows the shell frame and login surface state only, damage loop, shutdown path; no module pane.
S6: detached windows and per-monitor DPI; 100-cycle leak test against the MT-203 ledger.
